marks.gloss_en: הכי נמי מסתברא, דתנן: יתר עליהן אדם -- עיניו שתיהן גדולות שתיהן קטנות; in an animal both large/both small is no blemish (3b.7), so if change were the reason both should be; אלא לאו משום דהוה ליה שרוע (3b.8)
the stam's answer: no -- [one large eye] is a blemish because it is 'sarua' (an overgrown limb), not because of the change
לא, לעולם אימא לך משום שינוי, שינוי הוי מומא; both large / both small come from excess health or weakness, which would affect both eyes -- so the mishna's ruling does not show the reason is שרוע
והאמר רב יהודה: מותר לאדם להטיל מום בבכור קודם שיצא לאויר העולם! -- removing sanctity before birth is permitted (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)
התם מקדושת מזבח קא מפקע ליה, מקדושת כהן לא מפקע ליה; הכא אפילו מקדושת כהן קא מפקע ליה
Rav Yehuda: one may inflict a blemish on a firstborn before it emerges into the air of the world
R' Yochanan: [gentile partnership exempts] even in a part whose loss is a slight blemish
the slight-blemish dictum teaches like Rav Huna
the mishna (40a): its mouth resembling a pig's is a blemish
the mishna (40b): one eye large and one small [is a blemish]
a tanna: 'large' means as large as a calf's; 'small' as small as a goose's
of a person it is written 'any man of the seed of Aaron' (Lev 22:4) -- one equal to Aaron's seed; in an animal, both large or both small is no blemish
Rava to the convert: no one is concerned with R' Yehuda's view that gentile partnership is obligated in the firstborn
Rav Mari bar Rachel transferred the ears of [his firstborn fetuses] to a gentile, yet forbade them in shearing and work and gave them to priests -- and his animals died out
why did he transfer the ears at all? lest [the priests] come to a mishap with them
alternatively: Rav Mari knew to make a complete transfer; another would see him, do it [incompletely] thinking it is what Rav Mari did, and come to a mishap
אם פטרו את של ישראל במדבר, דין הוא שיפטרו את של עצמן -- if [the priests and Levites] exempted the Israelites' [firstborn] in the wilderness, it is only logical that they exempt their own
priests and Levites are exempt [from the firstborn of a donkey, the chapter's subject]
